{{AnimeLocationInfobox |name=Pericarp Town |characters=クムリタウン |japanese=Kumuri Town |image=Pericarp Town.png |imagesize=250px |caption=Pericarp Town |region=Unknown |epicode=HZ083 |episode=The Truth Revealed! |colorscheme=Paldea }} '''Pericarp Town''' (Japanese: '''クムリタウン''' ''Kumuri Town'') is an {{pkmn|animated series}}-exclusive location. It is located at the foot of [[Mount Pericarp]]. The scientific organization [[Exceed]] has established an outpost in the town. ==History== ===Pre-series=== 100 years prior to the events of the series, due to the [[Explorers]]'s arrival in [[Laqua]] atop the [[Mount Pericarp|mountain]], the [[Laquium]] there started growing and expanding and caused a huge explosion that blotted out the sun for three days and was felt all over the mountain, including Pericarp Town, which made many of the inhabitants, including a {{OBP|Matriarch|HZ084|3 year old girl}}, fear the [[Black Rayquaza]], that flew into the skies just after the explosion. A member of the Explorers named [[Gibeon]] managed to escape Laqua and eventually reach Pericarp Town, where his injuries were treated by the mother of the 3 year old girl. He then started living there and stablished the new Explorers's headquarters there to observe Laqua. ===''Pokémon Horizons: The Series''=== After gathering all of the [[Six Heroes]] in ''[[HZ083|The Truth Revealed!]]'', the [[Rising Volt Tacklers]] followed the [[Black Rayquaza]] on their [[Brave Olivine]] to [[Mount Pericarp]], where they landed on the mountain and [[Liko]], [[Roy]], [[Dot]], and [[Friede]] went to the Town to gather information about [[Laqua]]. In ''[[HZ084|Where the Land Meets the Sky]]'', the kids met [[Yuha]], a boy who believed that the Black Rayquaza would bring disaster, but after fighting off a swarm of {{p|Vibrava}} together, they convinced him that Rayquaza wasn't a bad sign. Meanwhile, Friede met the town's {{OBP|Matriarch|HZ084}}, an old woman who had seen the Black Rayquaza when she was little, giving him some important information about Gibeon and what happened in Laqua. The group then reunited and left the town to travel to Laqua. In [[HZ133]], the Rising Volt Tacklers and their allies fly pass Pericarp Town on their way to Laqua, which is seen by the townspeople and believed they were here to cause trouble until Yuha defended them. In the [[HZ134|next episode]], Pericarp Town became under attack by the Pokémon who live in town when the Laquium mist reached their area, as the townspeople are quick to blame the Rising Volt Tacklers. However, [[Ludlow]] as Mighty G, [[Orla]], [[Murdock]], and [[Mollie]] arrived in the Brave Olivine to help the townspeople alongside the Pokémon while [[Wy-Yes]] and [[Perrin]] take pictures. Seeing these actions, the townspeople start realizing that the Rising Volt Tacklers aren't bad guys, after all, much to the delight of Yuha. ==Pokémon seen in Pericarp Town== {| style="margin:auto; width: 30%" |- | {{InactivePoké|Pericarp Town|Turtonator|disp=Turtonator|Pericarp Town Turtonator.png|fire|dragon|link=no}} | {{InactivePoké|Pericarp Town|Crustle|disp=Crustle|Pericarp Town Crustle.png|bug|rock|link=no}} | {{InactivePoké|Pericarp Town|Sawsbuck|disp=Sawsbuck (x2)|Pericarp Town Sawsbuck.png|normal|grass|link=no}} |- | {{InactivePoké|Pericarp Town|Mandibuzz|disp=Mandibuzz|Pericarp Town Mandibuzz.png|dark|flying|link=no}} ♀ | {{InactivePoké|Pericarp Town|Spheal|disp=Spheal|Pericarp Town Spheal.png|ice|water|link=no}} | {{InactivePoké|Pericarp Town|Vibrava|disp=Vibrava (multiple)|Pericarp Town Vibrava.png|ground|dragon|link=no}} |} ==Names== {| class="roundtable" style="background:#{{scarlet color light}}; border:3px solid #{{scarlet color dark}}" |- ! style="background:#{{violet color light}}; color:#FFFFFF" | Language ! style="background:#{{violet color light}}; color:#FFFFFF" | Name ! style="background:#{{violet color light}}; color:#FFFFFF" | Origin |- | Japanese | クムリタウン ''Kumuri Town'' | From a partial anagram of ラクリウム ''Laqurium'' ([[Laquium]]) |- | English | Pericarp Town | From ''{{wp|Fruit (plant structure)#Pericarp layers|pericarp}}'' (outer layer of fruit enclosing the seed) |- | European Spanish,
